headline: Main Street Pothole Gains Own Yelp Page, Currently Rated 2.5 Stars
summary: Unrepaired road hazard accumulates 34 reviews ranging from 'disappointing depth' to 'surprisingly consistent.'
content:
The pothole at 412 Main Street, which first appeared following last winter's freeze-thaw cycle, has achieved what city infrastructure officials are calling "an unusual level of public engagement": its own Yelp business page with 34 reviews and a 2.5-star average rating.

The page, created by an anonymous user in December, lists the pothole under "Local Flavor" and "Landmarks & Historical Buildings." Its business hours are listed as "24/7, rain or shine."

Reviews range from the critical ("Nearly lost a hubcap. Very unprofessional.") to the philosophical ("Is it the pothole that is broken, or is it us?") to the surprisingly detailed ("Approximately 14 inches in diameter, 4 inches deep at center. Holds water well after rain. Three stars.").

One five-star review reads simply: "Been coming here for six months. Never changes. You can count on this pothole. That means something in today's world."

Public Works Director Samuel Chen confirmed the department is aware of both the pothole and its online presence. "We have a repair schedule based on severity and traffic impact," Chen explained. "This particular pothole is in the queue. The Yelp page doesn't change the timeline, but I'll admit it's... memorable."

When asked about the 2.5-star rating, Chen paused. "I mean, it's a pothole. What were people expecting? It's doing exactly what potholes do."

The page has also received three photos, including one captioned "My nemesis" and another showing a small traffic cone someone placed inside it with a handwritten sign reading "I tried."

Repairs are tentatively scheduled for spring.
author: Marcus Webb, Features Writer
